# Private generated files

GH-0601 created the server-side metadata and private-object boundary. GH-0602 adds its smallest
delivery capability: a project owner can receive a short-lived signed download URL only after the
server rechecks the trusted user, app, workspace and project scope.

## Public contract

`FileService` exposes `storeGenerated`, `list`, `get`, `softDelete` and `createDownload`. It accepts
a verified `TrustedOrganizationContext` plus generated bytes, project UUID, idempotency key,
original filename and MIME type. It never accepts an owner, organization, app, status, provider,
bucket, storage key, hash, capability, object version or requested URL lifetime from a consumer.

The owner-visible `FileRecord` contains only identifier, project, filename, MIME type, byte size,
sensitivity, ready state and timestamps. `createDownload` returns only an expiring URL and
`expiresAt`; it does not expose the storage provider, bucket, object key, content hash, capability,
idempotency fingerprint or object version.

## Lifecycle and isolation

Migration `0023` creates `hive.files` with an opaque database-generated key of the form
`ghf/<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>`. Original filenames are metadata only and are never
used as paths. Migration `0024` declares the exact `green-hive-generated` bucket as private,
extends the bounded Audit subject catalog with `FILE`, and adds a service-role-only audit writer.

```text
prepare (PROCESSING) -> private object write -> complete (READY)
                                                       |
                                                       v
owner scope recheck -> short signed URL -> audited return
                                                       |
                                                       v
                                                soft delete (DELETED)
```

Before signing, the service finds a `READY` row only under the verified owner/workspace/app/project
scope. It checks the configured provider and bucket, then asks the injected private-storage adapter
to create a server-owned 60–300 second grant. The lifetime is fixed in server configuration; it is
not browser input. The adapter verifies the persisted object version before signing. After a valid
URL is minted but before it is returned, `hive.record_file_export(...)` repeats the database scope
check and writes one `FILE_EXPORTED` event with only file ID, MIME type, byte size and sensitivity.
The URL, signed token, storage key, provider credential and content are never audited.

`authenticated` has no lifecycle or export-function grant, no direct file write and no
platform-admin bypass. A different user, a different app, a logically deleted file and a platform
administrator cannot obtain a download grant through this owner path.

## Storage adapters and operational activation

`FakeFileStorage` is deterministic, in-memory and zero-network; it creates opaque test URLs.
`SupabasePrivateStorageProvider` is an injected server-only adapter which accepts only configured
private buckets and opaque keys, reconciles object versions, and calls Supabase Storage's
short-lived signing operation. It accepts HTTPS URLs, or loopback HTTP only for local development.
Credentials and client construction remain outside the package and must never be browser-accessible.

The local stack starts Supabase Storage with the exact private bucket and keeps its container inside
the protected Docker network with no host-published port. `npm run files:storage:test:local` uses
the real server-only adapter to write a random opaque object, prove its public endpoint rejects the
read, obtain the exact short signed download through `FileService`, read the bytes once and remove
the object even after a failure. `npm run staging:files:storage:test` repeats that disposable gate
only against the explicitly confirmed dedicated staging project. Both gates passed; no bucket was
made public to do so.

## Deliberately deferred

GH-0602 does not add a browser upload endpoint, arbitrary user uploads, permanent public URLs,
download listing UI, malware scanning, content preview, CDN/cache delivery, generic rendering or a
worker. GH-0603 owns generic PDF/text rendering and storage composition.
